evidence: Raw HTTP exploit request, not a standalone JSP webshell. Its JSPX expression only displays the server time.
The first DWR call invokes SecurityService.isPasswordUppercase; the second invokes runWorkflowRule for AbCommonResources-writeHTMLtoFile.
The object binds html to c1-e1 and fileExtension to c1-e2; the latter is JSPX. This combines a privileged-session bypass attempt with creation of server-executable content.
Host and project are fixture placeholders. No successful live exploitation or arbitrary-command webshell is claimed.

evidence: Python CLI exploit client using the first positional argument as the target base URL.
Its POST batches the password-check/session-inheritance primitive with AbCommonResources-getDataRecords.
The fieldNames reference selects afm_users.user_name and afm_users.user_pwd; restriction 1=1 and recordLimit 10000 request a broad credential read.
The response is read, decoded, and printed. There is no separate attacker-controlled exfiltration endpoint or local payload execution.
An intercepted urllib.request.urlopen call confirmed the exact URL, POST body, and printed response without contacting a target.

evidence: Short Metasploit-style exploit scaffold; its declared name and default Meterpreter payload do not establish successful payload delivery.
The exploit method sends a normal GET to /wsproxy/?bmID=-3389&port=5984, then a separate PUT to /_config/query_servers/msf on the configured HTTP target.
There is no WebSocket upgrade, loopback host parameter, retained tunnel connection, or forwarding of the second request through the first.

The PUT data is a single-quoted Ruby string. The literal #{payload.encoded} is transmitted, not evaluated. A mocked execution confirmed both requests and would have failed on any attempted payload evaluation.
generate_cmdstager prepares a command list, but the result is unused. There is no execute_cmdstager, command delivery loop, or query/view activation request.

Retain a suspicious trait for the actual shell-valued configuration request. Under the requested concrete-behavior standard, the incomplete scaffold does not establish theft, spying, destruction, a working backdoor, or deception.

analysis_method: Full source and wire-format review, cleave facts including text/decoded-string facts, atomscan before/after, and network-intercepted Python/Ruby execution. No live exploit requests were sent.
obfuscation: None. URL-encoded page=%2F is protocol data; the Ruby interpolation marker is an inert literal, not decoded code.
dependencies: No fetched dependency is implicated; these are individual source/request artifacts. No dependent-package exception was introduced.
rule_changes: Replace a bare JSP-valued DWR argument with byte-checked fileExtension reference binding; reject unrelated arguments, identifier prefixes, and extension suffixes.

The inline-YARA rule and upload composite explicitly support Python, PowerShell, text, and JSP, within the validator four-type cap. Other original carriers retain the batch authentication-bypass coverage.
